headline: The world needs people who have come alive
universal_truth: Following your aliveness is not selfish—it's essential
fun_facts: People who regularly engage in activities that energize them report 31% higher life satisfaction
The concept of 'flow state'—being fully absorbed in an activity—was identified by psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi in the 1970s
Studies show that doing what you love activates the brain's reward system more powerfully than external rewards like money
discussion_questions: When do you lose track of time because you're so engaged?
What activities leave you more energized than when you started?
How might you create more space for what makes you come alive?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Howard Thurman said: Don't ask what the world needs. Ask what makes you come alive—because what the world needs is people who have come alive. Today we explore why this isn't selfish. It's essential.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Most people organize their lives around obligations, leaving aliveness for 'someday.' But here's the thing: aliveness isn't a luxury. What happens when we ignore what makes us come alive?
cliff.prompt: What happens when we ignore what energizes us?

options.text: We get by, but feel empty
options.response: Exactly. We survive, but we don't thrive. And eventually, that emptiness has consequences.
That's what we tell ourselves. But responsibility without renewal leads to burnout, not effectiveness.

q1.title: The Aliveness Signal
q1.script: Your sense of aliveness is information. When you feel energized, engaged, and fully present, your brain is telling you: this matters to you. It's not frivolous—it's a compass pointing toward your unique contribution. Ignoring it is ignoring yourself.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Aliveness Signal"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Flow and Fulfillment
q2.script: Psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi discovered that our happiest moments aren't passive or relaxing. They happen when we're stretched in a meaningful challenge—what he called flow. That absorbed, timeless feeling is aliveness in action.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Aliveness as Service
q3.script: Here's the twist: when you come alive, you have more to give. Your energy, creativity, and presence overflow to others. Martyrdom leads to resentment. Aliveness leads to generosity. The most giving people are often the most alive.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You don't find your aliveness by thinking about it. You find it by noticing when you feel most like yourself. Pay attention to those moments. They're breadcrumbs leading to your purpose.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's today's lesson on coming alive. Tomorrow, we'll explore why you get up each morning. Until then, notice what makes your heart beat a little faster.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Aliveness Inventory - Finding Your Fuel
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify activities and contexts that generate energy and aliveness
growTrack.activity: Make a list of 5 moments from the past month when you felt most alive. Look for patterns: what were you doing, who were you with, what made it special?
